<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. IX.|ACCORDING TO S. MATTHEW.|23}}</noinclude>fast? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=15}}† And IESVS sayd to them, Can the children of the bridegrome mourne, as long as the bridegrome is vvith them? But the dayes vvil come vvhen the bridegrome shal be taken avvay from them, and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Christ signifieth that the Churche shal vse fasting daies after his Ascension. ''Epiph. in Comp. fid. Cath. Aug. ep. 80''.}}∷ then they shal fast. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=16}}† And no body putteth a peece of ravv cloth to an old garment. For he taketh avvay the peecing therof from the garment, and there is made a greater rent. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=17}}† Neither do they put ‖ nevv vvine into old bottels. Othervvise the bottels breake, and the vvine runneth out, and the bottels perish. But nevv vvine they put into nevv bottels: and both are preserued together.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=18}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 5, 22. Luc. 8, 41.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Gospel vpō the 23 Sunday after Pentecost.}}∷ As he was speaking this vnto them, behold a certaine Gouernour approched, and adored him, saying, Lord, my daughter is euen novv dead: but come, lay thy hand vpon her, and she shal liue. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=19}}† And IESVS rysing vp folovved him, and his Disciples. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=20}}† And behold a vvoman vvhich vvas troubled vvith an issue of bloud ‖ tvvelue yeres, came behind him, and touched the hemme of his garment. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=21}}† For she sayd vvithin her self, If I shal ‖ touch only his garment: I shal be safe. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=22}}† But IESVS turning and seeing her, sayd, Haue a good hart daughter, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Loe, her deuotion to the hemme of his garment, was not superstition, but a token of greater faith: so is the deuout touching of holy relikes.}}∷ thy faith hath made the safe. And the woman became vvhole from that houre. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=23}}† And when IESVS vvas come into the house of the Gouernour, & savv minstrels and the multitude keeping a sturre, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=24}}† he sayd, Depart: for the vvenche is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed him to skorne. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=25}}† And vvhen the multitude vvas put forth, he entred in, and held her hand. And the mayde arose. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=26}}† And this bruite vvent forth into al that countrie.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=27}}† And as IESVS passed forth from thence, there folovved him tvvo blinde men crying and saying, Haue mercie on vs, O sonne of Dauid. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=28}}† And vvhen he vvas come to the house, the blinde came to him. And IESVS sayth to them, ‖ Do you beleeue, that I can doe this vnto you? They say to him, Yea Lord. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=29}}† Then he touched their eyes, saying, According to your faith, be it done to you. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=30}}† And their eyes vvere opened, and IESVS threatened them, saying, See that no man know it. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=31}}† But they vvent forth, & bruited him in al that countrey.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=32}}† And vvhen they vvere gone forth, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 12, 22.''}}* behold they brought him a dumme man, possessed vvith a diuel. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=33}}† And after the diuel vvas cast out, the dumme man spake, and the multitudes marueled saying, Neuer vvas the like seene in Israel.<noinclude>{{rh|||But}}</noinclude>
